title: Latency-entropy fallback controller and staged circuit policy
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Implement a novel fallback trigger that combines latency distribution entropy with percentile and error-rate signals to decide per-region and per-tenant circuit breaker state and staged fallback to model variants. Goal: reduce cascade failures and noisy churn from naively thresholded 95p-based triggers while keeping SLOs for latency and correctness. This controller will emit structured events so Console rollouts and routing can act deterministically (route to cheaper quantized variant, degrade streaming to batch mode, or route to Dedicated capacity). The design favors conservative open decisions with probabilistic probing for recovery and a short fast-path for emergency full-cutover.

Key design points: 
- Metric: compute sliding-window latency entropy (Shannon) per route/region/tenant over 60s windows, tracked alongside p50/p95/p99 and error-rate. Entropy spike indicates multimodal latency distributions (queueing + tail events) that precede capacity collapses.
- Trigger rule (initial): if entropy increases by >35% vs baseline AND (p95 > configured threshold OR error-rate > 2%), mark candidate for soft-open.
- Soft-open: limit new requests by probabilistic sampling (e.g., drop 15% of incoming requests for that tenant/route) and start golden-probe sampler (1% of requests routed to primary model and 99% to fallback variant) while ramping logging.
- Hard-open: if soft-open continues for 2 windows or error-rate increases, route to fallback variant or lower-cost quantized model and enable cooldown.
- Recovery: scheduled probes use an exponential backoff prober that increases probe fraction and checks both entropy and p95. Only fully close circuit if 3 consecutive probe windows pass.
- Observability: add a Grafana panel for entropy deltas, a heatmap for regional entropy, and alerting rules for sustained entropy > X and drift vs baseline.
- API/Config: expose per-tenant thresholds and three-policy presets (conservative, default, aggressive) plus an "emergency cutover" toggle for SRE.

Trade-offs and rationale: 
- Entropy gives early-warning for distributional shifts but is noisy; combining it with p95 and error-rate reduces false positives.
- Probabilistic soft-open avoids sudden global flux and keeps some traffic to the primary model for signal.
- We accept slightly higher complexity in telemetry to avoid frequent unnecessary model fallbacks that increase user-visible errors.

Required infra changes: new telemetry aggregator job to compute entropy, new routing flag for probabilistic sampling, changes to circuit state store (per-tenant, per-route), Console UI hooks for visualizing entropy-driven events.
acceptance_criteria: Entropy metric computed and emitted in metrics namespace: routing.latency_entropy (per route, region, tenant)
Controller implements soft-open and hard-open states with prober and cooldown logic
Routing supports probabilistic sampling and model-variant routing controlled by controller state
Grafana dashboard and alert rule for entropy deltas added and linked in ticket
E2E test that simulates a multimodal latency spike and verifies controller transitions and model fallback
Runbook drafted for SRE to inspect and revert emergency cutovers
